title: The Tax-to-GDP Signal: Fiscal Space or Composition Effect?
trigger: Eurostat’s 29 October release reported EU tax and net social contributions at 40.7% of GDP in 2025, up from 40.2% in 2024. Denmark recorded 44.3% and Sweden 41.2% in 2025.
limitations: The published tax-to-GDP ratio includes taxes and net social contributions; it is not a marginal tax rate. EU, EA20, Denmark and Sweden are not interchangeable jurisdictions. All GDP levels and shocks are illustrative and are not forecasts or budget projections.
formula: Reference receipts = hypothetical GDP × published 2025 tax-to-GDP ratio. Scenario receipts = GDP × (1 + nominal GDP shock) × (reference ratio + ratio shift). Change = scenario receipts − reference receipts. This is a mechanical accounting counterfactual, not a structural tax elasticity estimate.
decision: Separate cyclical revenue sensitivity from policy, compliance, base and composition effects. Evaluate expenditure commitments and debt-service dynamics before interpreting a tax-ratio increase as fiscal space.
worked_example: Illustrative worked example: at a hypothetical €500bn nominal GDP and the published EU 40.7% tax-to-GDP ratio, a 2% nominal GDP decline with an unchanged ratio mechanically reduces receipts by €4.07bn.
